provenance_note: The corpus was authored by another agent from the public specification and the cited standards without access to this code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Hand-built equipment datasheets covering the five spec presets (P1 pump NPSH margin, P2 equal-percentage control valve, P3 AHU revision B, P4 dry-type transformer overload, P5 emergency-standby generator set), nine clean baselines that between them exercise all eleven equipment templates (the AHU and generator-set templates are carried by P3, P5 and the EQU-R-150 near-miss instead), and a trigger plus a near-miss for every review rule EQU-R-001..151 that the corpus can express (identity and id collision, revision pattern and ranking, package cross-references, completeness at the three maturities, SI domains and display-unit lists, disabled-case slots, enum validity, the calculation trace of spec 4.9 in all five of its states, revision comparison and description rules, flags against the sheet and against linked requirements, and the consistency checks: design-pressure and design-temperature envelopes, driver and capacity rating with a user margin, NPSH margin per case, rated point inside the operating range, control-valve flow coefficient and 10-90 % opening band, counter-current temperature ordering, heat balance, tank level and capacity, and the three template scope limits). Expected values were written from SPEC-equipmentdatasheet.md revision 2026-09-22.1, as amended by adjudication to revision 2026-09-23.2 (EQU-R-140 limit, the spec 4.9 timestamp grammar and four clarifications), and computed by an own stdlib engine (equipmentdatasheet-ref.py) that implements the spec's unit table, epsilon comparisons, check types and rule triggers without seeing the tool; the engine is checked in selftest() against every number the spec states in sections 4.3-4.7 and 9. Standards are cited only where the corpus author verified them independently of the spec (IEC 60076-11:2018 scope, ISO 8528-1 rating categories, EN 13053:2019 title, IEC 60534-2-1:2011 scope and incompressible equation form, IEC 60034-1 duty-type clause, the API 610 12th edition data-sheet bulletin); the eleven parameter templates themselves are the spec's author method and are not benchmarked against any published form.
reference_citations: SPEC-equipmentdatasheet.md revision 2026-09-23.2 (originally authored against revision 2026-09-22.1) (_docs/SPEC-equipmentdatasheet.md), sections 2-9 and 12-15: the normative data model, unit table, check types, rule triggers, presets and corpus interface used for every expected value here; section 17 carries the adjudication changelog that changed the EQU-R-140 limit, defined "unparsable" in section 4.9 and gave the min-flow case of section 4.6 the same column-order tie-break as the max-flow case

IEC 60076-11:2018 Ed. 2.0 (2018-08-15), clause 1 scope, verified by the corpus author on the IEC webstore abstract (webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/29711): 'applies to dry-type power transformers (including auto-transformers) having values of highest voltage for equipment up to and including 72,5 kV and at least one winding operating at greater than 1,1 kV' — the basis and the inclusive boundary of EQU-R-141

ISO 8528-1:2018 power rating categories COP, PRP, LTP, ESP, DCP, verified by the corpus author through the Cummins 'Understanding ISO 8528-1 Generator Set Ratings' white paper (cummins.com, 2017): ESP is 'for supplying emergency power for the duration of a utility power failure', not to exceed 200 h/yr — the basis of EQU-R-150; the standard text itself was not read

EN 13053:2019, title verified by the corpus author on the SIS and BSI catalogue records: 'Ventilation for buildings — Air handling units — Rating and performance for units, components and sections'; no clause of it is used, and the T3 parameter list is author method, as the spec states

IEC 60534-2-1:2011 Ed. 2.0, clause 1 scope and the incompressible turbulent form Q = C N1 Fp sqrt(dp_sizing/(rho1/rho0)), verified by the corpus author on the iteh.ai preview (cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/15856/): the standard excludes non-Newtonian fluids, mixtures, slurries and multiphase streams, which is why the spec's limitation 4 restricts the valve check to liquid. With C = Av, N1 = 1 in SI base units and Fp = 1 the form reduces to Av = Q sqrt(rho/dp), the expression of spec 4.6

IEC 60034-1 duty types: clause 4.2.1 'Duty type S1 — Continuous running duty', verified by the corpus author on the ANSI webstore preview of Ed. 15.0 (2026-03), which carries the same clause numbering as the Ed. 14.0 (2022-02) the spec cites — the basis of EQU-R-151

API 610 12th edition data sheet practice, verified by the corpus author through the Amarinth technical bulletin (amarinth.com/media/API-610-12th-Edition.pdf): 'text in Black is for the purchaser to complete; text in Blue for the supplier to complete', NPSH3 values required at test points 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8, end of curve at 120 % of BEP flow — the secondary basis of the purchaser/supplier split that the spec maps onto the enquiry/order maturities and of the NPSH3 naming; the standard text itself was not read

API 650 internal-pressure practice (2,5 psig), secondary sources only, as the spec declares: EQU-R-140 is author method and its limit is 2,5 psi converted through the factor 6894,757293168 of spec 3.2, 17 236,893 232 92 Pa (2,5 psi through the exact factor of spec 3.2). Adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1) replaced the earlier rounded 17 236,89 Pa, which made a tank entered at exactly 2,5 psi trip the rule. The inclusive reading of the 2,5 psig limit ("operating pressures <= 2.5 psig", "not exceeding 2.5 psig") was re-verified by the adjudicator on authorizedinspector.com/asme-api-650-tank-calculations/, secondary as before.

Kv/Cv relation Cv = 1,156 Kv, i.e. Kv = 0,865 Cv, the commonly published rounded factor (engineeringtoolbox-class sources); the spec declares it author method and the corpus only asserts the arithmetic that follows from the factor as written in spec 3.2
tolerance: Categorical outputs are exact: the fired set (rule id plus target), the verdict, the four severity counts, save_refused, candidate_id, the changed set, worst_case, max_flow_case, min_flow_case, next_rev and every integer count — all are discrete outcomes of boolean and string rules, so any deviation is a defect, not rounding. Numeric tolerances are derived from the arithmetic, not chosen to pass: si.<slot> carries relative 1e-12 because a stored value is one multiplication and one addition (SI = a x display + b) on the exact factors of spec 3.2, so about 2 ulp of double; RATING D/Req/margin_actual, NPSH diff, VALVE kv_req/phi/h, and BALANCE r carry relative 1e-9 (absolute 1e-9 when the reference is 0) because spec 13.2 sets that figure and because each is a closed-form chain of at most six double operations (a square root, two divisions, a logarithm), four orders of magnitude above their rounding. 1e-9 is also the tool's own comparison epsilon, so every boundary case here places its operands either exactly on the limit (40 degC against 40 degC, h = 0,10, r = 0,01, R = D, Um = 72 500 V, 1000 V, level 12 m = 12 m) or clearly off it (5e-9 and 5e-10 relative for the EQU-R-033 pair, 5e-9 and 5e-10 relative either side of the epsilon for EQU-R-033), never inside the epsilon band where the outcome would be a matter of rounding. Cases whose expected value depends on a disputable reading of the spec are marked disputable: true on the affected check and are listed in coverage.ambiguities.

coverage.summary: 105 cases: 5 spec presets, 9 clean per-template baselines, and trigger/near-miss pairs for 50 of the 51 rules (EQU-R-060 is excluded by spec 14, see not_benchmarked). Boundary cases sit exactly on every equality the spec names: GE/LE at equality (design pressure, design temperature, ambient temperature, rated flow at the range end, R = D, Req = R, NPSH diff = margin, Um = 72,5 kV, rated voltage = 1000 V, tank level and capacity, p_design at exactly 2,5 psi), LT failing at equality (terminal temperature cross, chilled-water temperatures), BALANCE passing at exactly 0,01, valve openings passing at exactly 0,10 and 0,90, phi exactly 1, the absolute-vacuum and absolute-zero domain edges, the two-letter and two-digit revision limits, and REL_DIFF at 5e-10 and 5e-9 either side of the 1e-9 epsilon. Fifteen cases marked "added by adjudication" close holes independent review found against the spec. The first pass added seven: RATING with D = 0 (spec 4.2), REL_DIFF with s(a,b) = 0 (spec 4.1), the worst_case column-order tie (spec 4.2), the valve max-flow tie with no min-flow case (spec 4.6), eight display units of spec 3.2 no case converted, EQU-R-010 at the as-built maturity, and the offset form of an ISO-8601 instant (spec 4.9 as amended). The second pass added eight: the spec 5.3.2 suppression measured on a numeric slot that is an operand of a check (an invalid t_pump leaves LE_MIN and does not also raise EQU-R-010), next('ZZ') = 'AAA' (the one value spec 4.8 names that no case asserted), the min-flow case tie (spec 4.6 as amended, changelog entry 6), and five conversion cases that take the graded display-unit ids of spec 3.2 from 29 of 47 to 45 of 47 (A, rad/s, V, Hz, m, '-', VA, kVA, MVA, m3/s, Pa.s, mPa.s, kg/m3, mm, L/s and h). kg/s and s remain ungraded: both are identity factors (a = 1, b = 0) on dimensions already graded at two non-identity factors each (mass_flow at t/h = 1/3,6 and kg/h = 1/3600, time at min = 60 and h = 3600); kg/s is entered, unasserted, in existing cases.
ambiguities: Spec 3.4 abbreviates the display-unit list of most case parameters as 'm3/h, ...' and 'bar, ...'. The corpus reads the ellipsis as the same ordered list the first full row of that dimension gives (vol_flow m3/h, m3/s, L/s, USgpm; pressure bar, kPa, MPa, psi, Pa; temperature degC, K, degF). Only the EQU-R-012 cases depend on this, and they use the explicit pump p_design row.

Spec 4.10 defines required_present without saying whether a slot that is present but invalid (EQU-R-011 or EQU-R-014) counts. The corpus counts it as present, because spec 5.3.2 says such a slot 'is present but invalid; it is not also missing'. Case r014-invalid-enum-not-also-missing is the one that depends on the reading.

Spec 4.2 said worst_case is the first case in column order 'attaining D'. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1): 'attaining D' is exact equality with D, the reading the corpus already used. Case adj-rating-worst-case-tie-first-column puts two cases on the same double and asserts the earlier column.

Spec 4.8 gives next(rev) for letters (A->B, Z->AA) and digits (n->n+1) but not what happens when the result leaves the valid pattern: next('99') = '100' and next('ZZ') = 'AAA' both fail EQU-R-004. Case r004-nm-two-digits asserts next('99') = '100' as the literal reading and notes that the tool would then report its own new revision as invalid. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1): next() is computed on the bijective sequence whatever the result looks like, and a result outside the EQU-R-004 pattern then fires EQU-R-004 - the reading the corpus already used.

EQU-R-140's limit was written as 17 236,89 Pa while the secondary source the spec cites gives 2,5 psi = 17 236,893232... Pa, so a design pressure entered as exactly 2,5 psi fired the rule. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1): spec 3.4 T7 and spec 5.2 now state the limit as 2,5 psi converted through the factor of spec 3.2, 17 236,893 232 92 Pa (2,5 psi through the exact factor of spec 3.2), and case r140-tank-design-pressure-entered-as-2-5-psi now expects no finding.

Spec 3.4 lists the T9 poles and T10 insulation_temp enum members as bare numbers while spec 3.1 stores enum values as strings. The corpus writes them as strings ('2', '155'); a tool storing them as numbers would need the comparison to be type-tolerant.

EQU-R-012 is defined as 'display_units[key] set AND not in that parameter's allowed list'. The spec does not say what happens when the key is not a parameter of the current template at all. The corpus does not evaluate the rule there, consistent with spec 3.1's rule that a non-template slot is kept but not evaluated.

Spec 4.2 says a check 'runs only when every operand it needs is present'. For RATING this leaves open whether the margin counts as a needed operand; the corpus reads it as optional (EQU-R-105 exists precisely to report its absence) and evaluates the overload branch without it, which spec 4.2 states explicitly a paragraph later.

Spec 5.2 wrote the EQU-R-120 trigger as 'phi_c > 1 + eps' with an explicit epsilon rather than through the GE/LE helpers of spec 4.1. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1): the trigger is NOT LE(phi_c, 1), the ordinary epsilon comparison. The two readings differ only for phi within about 1e-9 of 1 and case r120-nm-flow-coefficient-exactly-rated, where phi is exactly 1, expects no finding under either.

Spec 4.9 said an unparsable attached_at counts as changed without naming a parser, so a zone-less string such as '2026-09-20 09:00' could be read as a local time and make the staleness verdict depend on the reader's time zone. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.1): only the ISO-8601 instant forms are parsable; everything else, zone-less strings included, is unparsable and counts as changed. Cases r031-unparsable-timestamp and adj-r031-nm-offset-timestamp-same-instant bracket the decision.

Spec 4.6 fixed a tie-break for the max-flow case ('first in column order on a tie') but not for the min-flow case, although the min-flow case decides where EQU-R-122 is evaluated. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.2, changelog entry 6): the same column-order tie-break applies to both, so with q tied between normal and minimum the min-flow case is normal. Case adj-valve-min-flow-case-tie pins it; tool and reference engine already agreed on this reading, so no expected value changed.

Spec 4.10 defined 'tightest' as the passing RATING / NPSH instance with the smallest normalised headroom (R - Req)/Req resp. (diff - m)/max(m, 1e-30) without saying whether an instance with no margin (one that raised EQU-R-105 or EQU-R-108) is a candidate. RESOLVED by adjudication (spec rev 2026-09-23.2, changelog entry 7): it is not, because Req = (1 + m) x D does not exist without m, and 'tightest' is null when no instance qualifies. No corpus value changes: spec 13.2 still does not list the field, so it stays unasserted.

not_benchmarked: EQU-R-060 (permalink longer than 4096 characters): spec 14 excludes it because the length depends on the encoder, not on this spec; the corpus can express neither a trigger nor a near-miss for it in the vocabulary of spec 13.1. It is the one rule of the 51 with no case.

Completeness of the eleven parameter templates against published datasheet forms (spec 14; the forms are protected and the templates are declared author method). The corpus asserts the behaviour of the parameters it uses, not that the lists are complete.
Numerical correctness of pulled calculation values: they belong to the source tool's own benchmark (spec 14). The corpus only asserts the trace, the conversion and the staleness state.
UI layout, the utilisation figure, PDF pagination and the seven-language wording (spec 14): browser QA, not corpus.

Package transport behaviour — round trip, unknown sections kept verbatim, byte-identical write-back of other register items, storage that throws (spec 14 and acceptance criteria 9, 11, 18): these need a live DiagramProject runtime. The corpus asserts only the rules that read a loaded section.
Gas, steam, two-phase, flashing, cavitating and choked valve sizing, installed characteristic and noise; multi-pass F-factor correction and any heat-exchanger thermal design (limitations 4 and 5).

The Python export file and its self-test as artefacts: the quantities it covers (rating, npsh, valve, balance, order and the per-instance pass/fail booleans) are asserted through the case outputs instead.

The 'tightest passing margin' of spec 4.10: spec 13.2 does not list it among the checkable outputs, so the corpus asserts no value for it. The reading is no longer open — spec rev 2026-09-23.2, changelog entry 7, says only an instance whose margin is present can be the tightest, because without the margin there is no Req and no headroom — but grading it would need spec 13.2 to name it.

Ordering of the findings list (spec 5.3.5): the corpus compares fired as a set, because the spec's tie-break 'target in template order' is not defined for targets that are not slots (check: and flag: targets).

RATING margin_actual when D = 0: spec 4.2 says it is "not defined" and spec 13.2 gives no value for that state, so case adj-rating-demand-zero asserts D and worst_case and leaves margin_actual unasserted.

Graded conversion of the display units kg/s (mass_flow) and s (time): both are identity factors (a = 1, b = 0) on dimensions whose non-identity factors are graded elsewhere (t/h = 1/3,6 and kg/h = 1/3600 in adj-si-unit-table-second-half; min = 60 in si-pump-imperial-and-mixed-units and h = 3600 in adj-si-genset-autonomy-in-hours). kg/s is entered in existing cases, so a template that refused it would fail on EQU-R-012; only the arithmetic is left unasserted. 45 of the 47 display-unit ids of spec 3.2 carry a graded si.<slot> assertion.

EQU-R-121 at exactly 0,10 on the max-flow case: the opening is a quotient of two computed doubles, and no input the corpus can express places it exactly on 0,10 rather than within the 1e-9 epsilon that spec 13.2 warns against. The 0,90 edge of the same rule is exact (r121-nm-opening-exactly-ninety-percent) and the 0,10 edge is exact on the min-flow case (r122-nm-min-flow-exactly-ten-percent).
